On 26th January 1950, the Preamble (originally) declared India a Sovereign Democratic Republic. Later this was amended by the 42nd CA (1976) which added the words Socialist and Secular.
Decoration by: Beohar Ram Manohar Sinha, Nand Lal Bose.
Language of Preamble: taken from Australia.
In the case of 'Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay v. Union of India (Nov, 2024) the Supreme Court rejected the petition challenging the insertion of "Socialist" and "Secular" into the preamble.
It is an introductory statement in a Constitution, which states the reasons and guiding values of the Constitution.
It contains the summary or the essence of the Constitution.
It tells us about the philosophy of the Constitution.
It was made after the entire Constitution was compiled.
It is a modified version of the Objective Resolution presented by J.L. Nehru before the Constituent Assembly.

blocks.text: Nature of the Constitution SOVEREIGN
People have supreme right to make decisions on internal as well as external matters. No external power can dictate the government of India.
Wealth is generated socially and should be shared equally by society.
Government should regulate the ownership of land and industry to reduce socio-economic inequalities.
Example: Russia + Capitalistic: USA
The term 'Socialism' derives its inspiration from the Russian Revolution.
Types of Socialism:
Radical Socialism: The idea of ending private ownership of businesses and wealth and making everything shared so that everyone is equal (Classless Society).
Gandhian Socialism: A system promoting Non-violence, Self-reliance and fair wealth distribution through village- centered economy.
Nehruism Socialism: A system emphasizing state- controlled development to achieve economic growth and social equality. It is also known as Mixed Socialism.
Citizens have complete freedom to follow any religion or no religion at all. There is no official state religion.
Government treats all religious beliefs and practices equally and impartially.
In India, secularism follows a positive concept.
(Involvement of state in religious matters).
The government functions according to a set of constitutional rules and principles.
A Government Of the People, By the People, For the People-As said by Abraham Lincoln
Democracy means a system of 'Government by consent'- John Locke (Father of Liberalism). Book- ' Two Treatises of Government' 1689.
Direct Democracy: A form of government in which citizens directly participate in the decision-making process and vote on laws and policies themselves.
(Eg:- Switzerland, Uruguay, Latvia, Lithuania etc).
Indirect Democracy (Representative Democracy): A form of government in which citizens elect representatives who make laws and take decisions on their behalf. (Eg:- Canada, India, USA, UK, etc).
A system of government in which the head of the state is elected by the people and not based on a hereditary succession.
Objectives of the Constitution JUSTICE
Citizens cannot be discriminated on the grounds of caste, religion, and gender. Social inequalities have to be reduced.
Three types of justice are given in Preamble: Social, Economic and Political LIBERTY
There are no unreasonable restrictions on a citizen in what they think, how they wish to express their thoughts and the way they wish to follow up their thoughts in action.
Five forms of liberty are given in Preamble: Thought, Expression, Belief, Faith, and Worship EQUALITY
All are equal before the law. The traditional social inequalities must end. The government should ensure equal opportunities for all.
Two types of equality are given in Preamble: Status and Opportunity.
All of us should behave as if we are members of the same family. No one should treat a fellow citizen as inferior.
The terms "Liberty, Equality, Fraternity and Republic' are taken from France and the Ideals of Justice are taken from Russia.
Is Preamble a Part of Constitution and is it Amendable?
Berubari Union Case: 1960
Supreme Court held that- i) The Preamble is not a part of the Constitution & hence cannot be amended.; ii) It is just a key to understanding the Constitution. iii) It is not legally enforceable.
Kesavananda Bharati Case: 1973

In this case, Supreme Court Overruled the Berubari view and held that — i) The Preamble is a part of the Constitution and hence can be amended under Article 368. ii) It reflects the basic structure of the Constitution (decided by the Supreme Court).
LIC of India Case: 1995 i) Reaffirmed the Kesavananda Bharati case ruling.
Preamble has been amended only once in 1976 through 42nd Constitutional Amendment. a Gee aay ote al It added the terms: Integrity, Socialist, Secular (TRICK: ISS/SIS)
Enforceability of Preamble
It is not enforceable in the Court of Law.
It is neither a source of Power nor Restriction to the legislature, but it can be considered as an aid to the legal interpretation of the Constitution.
